messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: prod/redwood-api high latency spike detected. metric: p95 increased from ~120ms -> ~620ms over last 5m. error-rate stable. paging oncall.
Erin (oncall): On it. Paging SREs. First pass: is this global or region-specific?
Mateo (sre): Seeing spikes in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. ap-south looks fine. Correlating deploy windows now.
Priya (infra): No deploys in last 30m from CI. Noted a kernel security patch roll yesterday on a subset of hosts (linux-5.19.3 -> 5.19.4) for image-builder pool.
Jin (perf): Can you paste p50/p95 times? I want distribution.
Erin (oncall): Short window numbers: p50 ~140ms (slightly up), p95 ~620ms, p99 ~1.2s. Request rate ~steady. CPU not saturated.
Mateo (sre): Adding traces. trace-bot: collected spans for sample requests -> https://traces.internal/r/abcd1234
trace-bot: linked trace bundle -> https://traces.internal/bundle/3345678901
Jin (perf): Skimming spans: long blocking in scheduling/softirq on a few spans; several spans show wait on /dev/nvme0 -> iowait spikes.
Priya (infra): Pulling perf counters from affected hosts: softirq: +2.3x, context-switches: +1.8x, cpu_idle down ~10%. Sharing logs: gs://redwood-logs/incidents/3345678901/
Sara (ops): Customer impact: noticing latency alerts from 4 customers on hosted tier. CSM Alex looped in.
Alex (CSM): I've notified the major customers with short note: "We're investigating an elevated latency incident; no data loss; will update in 30m." They asked about failover options.
Erin (oncall): Quick mitigation idea: toggle routing to healthy region (ap-south) for affected customers that can be moved. Mateo, can we policy-route? Also consider temporarily increasing instance counts.
Mateo (sre): Can do region failover for non-US customers. Pushing emergency routing to 50% for traffic matching non-enterprise keys: /api/v1/generate -> policy alpha.
Priya (infra): I'm rolling out a kernel rollback on 10% of the affected pool to 5.19.3 for canary. Command: 
```
sudo apt-get install linux-image-5.19.3 && sudo reboot
```
Tracking rollout in infra dashboard.
Jin (perf): After routing to ap-south, p95 dropped from 620ms -> 200ms for routed requests. The rollback canary hosts still show p95 ~140ms (good). Suggests kernel change correlates.
Erin (oncall): Mateo: keep routing. Priya: expand rollback if canary stays healthy. Jin: collect perf counter diffs pre/post rollback.
Mateo (sre): Routing now at 65% for non-enterprise. Monitoring.
Priya (infra): Canary rollback successful on 12 hosts. No regression observed in canary over 10m. Preparing staged rollback to 50%.
trace-bot: Raw span ids for problematic traces: span ids [s-88a1, s-88a2, s-88a3], exported to https://traces.internal/export/3345678901
Jin (perf): Perf counter snapshot (affected host vs rollback host): 
```
affected: softirq/sec=9800, ctx_switches/sec=42000, iowait=12.3%
rollback:   softirq/sec=4100, ctx_switches/sec=23000, iowait=2.1%
```
Jin (perf): Kernel scheduler and NVMe I/O path look implicated. There was a regressed preemption path in 5.19.4 per changelog (commit: c23f9e - rq_update tweak).
Priya (infra): Opening infra-ops ticket to track full pool rollback. tag: infra/rollback-3345678901
Mateo (sre): I'm compiling timeline for RCA: initial spike 3345678800, routing change 3345679120, canary rollback 3345679300, p95 improvement observed 3345679420.
Erin (oncall): Customer update: sent a follow-up with ETA ~1h for resolution and steps taken. No customer data exposure.
Alex (CSM): Customers replied: appreciate the update; one asks for postmortem—will share once RCA done.
Sara (ops): Any immediate mitigations left? We should keep scaled routing and finish rollback.
Priya (infra): Rolling rollback to 60% now. Will monitor for regressions.
Jin (perf): Next steps for RCA: collect perf profiles, kernel oops/noise logs, nvme driver trace, and full traces for 200 sample requests around spike. I'll draft hypotheses in thread:
- H1: kernel change (5.19.4) introduced scheduler path regression causing elevated softirq/iowait under our IO pattern.
- H2: NVMe driver tweak + kernel causes lock contention on nvme-queue leading to tail latency.
- H3: unrelated flash firmware flakiness (less likely given canary rollback effect).
Mateo (sre): Assigning owners: Jin -> perf trace analysis; Priya -> rollback automation; Erin -> customer comms; Mateo -> RCA doc/timeline.
Erin (oncall): If rollback to 100% clears p95, we'll treat as mitigation and preserve evidence (logs/traces) before any further reboots.
trace-bot: Exported all trace bundles and attached to ticket infra/rollback-3345678901: https://traces.internal/attach/3345678901
Priya (infra): Rollback at 75% complete. No new regressions observed in 15m window.
Mateo (sre): Observed system-wide p95 now ~160ms. Marking incident as mitigated for immediate customer impact. Will keep monitoring for 1h before declaring resolved.
Erin (oncall): Closing slack page for active paging but keeping thread live for RCA coordination. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
Jin (perf): I'll post a short RCA draft within 4h with perf counters and recommended kernel pin/patch blocking.
Alex (CSM): I'll prepare customer postmortem summary once you share the RCA draft.
Sara (ops): Recording playbook updates: add kernel patch gating for infra image-builder pipeline.
Mateo (sre): RCA doc link (placeholder): https://docs.internal/rca/3345678901 - will populate.
Erin (oncall): End of active mitigation. Monitoring window started. "last_ack": 3345679472."
